title: Interior Designer Salary: Hourly to Annual Pay in Australia
description: Understand interior designer salary in Australia. Convert hourly rates to annual pay using 38-hour week, 52 weeks. Includes tax, super, award coverage, and minimum wage.
salarySummary: The median interior designer salary is $1,692 per week ($42 per hour) based on ABS data, but pay varies by award coverage and experience; award-free designers receive at least the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour.

faqs.q: What is the average interior designer salary in Australia?
faqs.a: According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Survey of Employee Earnings and Hours, May 2025, the median full-time interior designer earns $1,692 per week before tax, or about $42 per hour. This is below the average full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week. Actual pay depends on qualifications, experience, award coverage, and whether you work full-time, part-time, or casually.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52 = annual gross salary. For example, $42 per hour × 38 × 52 = $82,992 per year. Your fortnightly pay is your weekly pay multiplied by 2. Remember that superannuation (12%) is paid on top of your ordinary earnings, not deducted from your salary.

faqs.q: What is the minimum wage for an interior designer?
faqs.a: From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour ($1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). If you are an interior designer who is award-free (e.g., you hold a degree and use it in your role), this is your minimum entitlement. If you are covered by an award, such as the Retail Award or Miscellaneous Award, the award rate may be higher. Casual employees receive at least a 25% loading on top of the base rate, making the minimum casual rate $33.05 per hour.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Convert an Interior Designer Hourly Rate to Annual Salary

If you're an interior designer or considering a career in interior design, understanding how your hourly rate translates to an annual salary is essential for budgeting, negotiating, and comparing job offers. The standard conversion used across Australia is:

**Annual gross salary = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For full-time work, we assume a 38-hour week, as this is the ordinary hours benchmark under the National Employment Standards. If you work part-time or casual hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. Your fortnightly pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by 2 — useful for planning regular expenses.

This calculation assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates or allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It gives you a consistent baseline to work from.

## Interior Designer Salary: What the Data Shows

According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Survey of Employee Earnings and Hours (May 2025), the median full-time interior designer earns **$1,692 per week** before tax, or about **$42 per hour**. This is based on a 43-hour average full-time week for the occupation. However, the ABS Average Weekly Earnings (May 2026) for all full-time adult ordinary time employees is **$2,083.70 per week**, indicating that interior designers typically earn below the national average for full-time workers.

It's important to note that these figures are medians — half of interior designers earn more, half earn less. Your actual pay will depend on your qualifications, experience, location, and the type of employer.

## Award Coverage for Interior Designers

Not all interior designers are covered by the same pay rules. The Fair Work Ombudsman explains that interior designers, decorators, and stylists may be:

- **Award-free** if they hold a degree qualification (e.g., Bachelor of Interior Design) and use it in their role. Award-free employees are entitled to the National Minimum Wage and the National Employment Standards.
- **Covered by an industry award** if their employer operates in a specific industry, such as retail (Retail Award) or manufacturing (Manufacturing Award for draughtspersons).
- **Covered by an occupational award** if they are registered architects (Architects Award) or professional engineers (Professionals Award).
- **Covered by the Miscellaneous Award** if they are unqualified or trade-qualified and not covered by another award.

For the majority of interior designers with a degree, award-free status is common. This means your minimum pay is the National Minimum Wage, unless your employer has an enterprise agreement that sets higher rates.

## National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the **National Minimum Wage** is:
- **$26.44 per hour**
- **$1,004.90 per week** for 38 hours

Award minimum wages also increased by 4.75% from the same date. If you are covered by an award, check the relevant pay guide for your classification. For example, the Retail Award may have higher rates for experienced interior designers working in retail settings.

## Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you work as a casual interior designer, you are entitled to a **25% casual loading** on top of the base hourly rate. For the National Minimum Wage, this means a minimum casual rate of **$33.05 per hour**. The loading compensates for the lack of paid leave and other entitlements. When using a calculator, never include the casual loading in your base rate — instead, add it separately.

**Superannuation** is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is **12%**, up to the maximum contribution base of **$270,830 per year**. Super is not deducted from your salary; it is an additional benefit. For example, on a $42 per hour rate, your employer would contribute an extra $5.04 per hour (12% of $42) to your super fund.

## Tax on Your Interior Designer Salary

Once you have your annual gross salary, you can estimate your take-home pay using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a **Medicare levy** of 2% of your taxable income (with reductions for low-income earners). The tax-free threshold is included. Note that HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not considered in this estimate.

## Putting It All Together: Example

Let's take a typical interior designer earning the median hourly rate of **$42 per hour**, working 38 hours per week:

- **Weekly gross**: $42 × 38 = $1,596
- **Fortnightly gross**: $1,596 × 2 = $3,192
- **Annual gross**: $1,596 × 52 = $82,992

Using the 2026–27 tax rates and Medicare levy (2%), the estimated annual tax is approximately $16,798, leaving a **take-home pay of about $66,194 per year** (or $1,273 per week).

Your employer would also pay **$9,959 in superannuation** (12% of $82,992) on top of your salary.

If you were award-free and earning the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour:

- **Annual gross**: $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245
- **Fortnightly gross**: $2,009.80
- **Estimated take-home**: around $43,000 per year after tax and Medicare
- **Super on top**: $6,269

## Using the Timesheet and Other Tools

To quickly convert your own hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, or weekly figures, use [the timesheet](/) on this site. You can also explore [pay guides](/blog) for award-specific rates, [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) calculations, and [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) details. For a deeper look at how your salary compares, see [average pay](/topics/average-pay) data from the ABS.

Remember that the figures here are estimates. Your actual pay and conditions depend on your award coverage, enterprise agreement, or individual contract. Always check with the Fair Work Ombudsman or your employer for precise entitlements.

## Key Takeaways

- The median interior designer salary is about **$42 per hour** or **$1,692 per week** full-time.
- The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is **$26.44 per hour** for award-free workers.
- Casual interior designers receive at least **$33.05 per hour** including the 25% loading.
- Superannuation of **12%** is paid on top of ordinary earnings.
- Use the formula **hourly × 38 × 52** for a standard full-time annual salary.

For more detailed information on award coverage, visit the Fair Work Ombudsman's award coverage page for interior designers and the pay guides page for current rates. The Jobs and Skills Australia profile provides additional earnings data.
